newsitem.title: USA: U.S. says Viet debt accord aids normal ties.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says Viet debt accord aids normal ties.

text.p: Vietnam's agreement to repay debt owed to the United States from the Vietnam War era will help speed normalised relations between the two countries, the State Department said on Tuesday.

"What's significant about it is it helps propel us down the road to normalisation of our economic relationships ... with the Vietnamese government," spokesman Nicholas Burns said of the agreement the United States and Vietnam initialed in Hanoi on Friday, ending several years of negotiations.

Under it, Vietnam will repay "all of its economic and social debt to the United States, which totals approximately $145 million," Burns said. It implements a rescheduling of Vietnam's debt to other countries decided in December 1993 by the Paris Club, a group of major countries that deals with the rescheduling of government-to-government debt.
The U.S. debt reflects four Agency for International Development loans and two loans under the PL-480 food programme to the government of South Vietnam during the Vietnam War era.

Three of the four AID loans were made in 1960-61 for physical infrastructure projects in Saigon, South Vietnam's capital. The fourth was made in 1973 to finance the import of U.S. commodities to South Vietnam. The food aid loans were also extended toward the end of the war, in 1973-74.
The U.S.-backed South Vietnamese government fell to the forces of the communist North in 1975.

President Bill Clinton established diplomatic relations with a united Vietnam in July 1995 and then-Secretary of State Warren Christopher visited the country in August of that year to raise the flag at the new American Embassy in Hanoi.

Since that time, the two countries have been negotiating over the many ways in which the Vietnamese economy must change before the administration is ready to grant most-favoured nation trading status to Hanoi. But talks have been slow because Vietnam still maintains many trade barriers.
